simple.meaning: מְשׁוֹאָה (mᵉshôwʼâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “(a) ruin , abstractly (the act) or concretely (the wreck).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Job, Zephaniah, beginning at Job 30:3. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְשׁוֹאָה (H4875).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מְשׁוֹאָה (mᵉshôwʼâh) / H4875 is traced through Job 30:3, Job 38:27, Zephaniah 1:15 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4875. meshoah מְשֹׁאָה מְשׁוֺאָה, noun feminine desolation ; — 1 singular only in וּמ ׳שֹׁאָה Zeph 1:15 ; Job 30:3 ; 38:27 , see foregoing; plural ( מַשּׁוּאוֺת , read) מְשׁוֺאוֺת , so Klo Hup-Now Che Comm. Bae Du Psa 74:3 ruins (of temple) and 73:18 ruins (of one's life, figurative; but Du here derives from נשׁא : deceptions ; yet compare synonym שַׁמָּה 73:19 ).
